meta.title: The signs we live by
meta.summary: A sign catches your eye and can hold a whole street’s memory. Cincinnati has saved plenty of them. ♡

blocks.text: In Cincinnati’s Camp Washington neighborhood, the American Sign Museum gathers more than a century of signs and signmaking history. Its collection includes signs, photographs, artworks, tools, and materials. I’d follow the lettering first: a shop sign gets only a moment to point passersby in the right direction, so its maker has to choose color, shape, scale, and light with care. Indoors, each sign also remembers a business and the street around it.

The museum's Main Street display lets signs speak to one another across styles and decades. There's a working neon shop in the building too, where visitors can sometimes watch a tube being bent or repaired. I like that link between preservation and continuing skill. Look closely at a painted letter or illuminated curve, then notice the signs on your own route home. They may never seem quite so ordinary again.
